content: Normochromic anemia, also referred to as normocytic anemia, is a frequently encountered hematological condition, particularly in individuals over the age of 85. Its prevalence increases significantly with advancing age, affecting approximately 44% of men older than 85 years. This type of anemia is the most commonly observed form of anemia in clinical practice. Normocytic anemia can arise from a variety of underlying causes. These include chronic diseases, acute blood loss, hemolysis, bone marrow disorders, or conditions associated with pregnancy and fluid overload. Additionally, it may result from a combination of factors that simultaneously produce microcytic and macrocytic anemia. To accurately differentiate normochromic anemia from other types of anemia or related diseases, a thorough review of the differential diagnosis is essential.
